best_for: People leaving uTorrent who want a free BitTorrent client with no ads, a built-in search, RSS rules and a web interface for a home server.

points.title: No ads, no bundled extras
points.text: qBittorrent is free under GPL-3.0, built by volunteers, and shows no ads. It aims to be an open-source replacement for uTorrent and looks much like it.

points.title: Search, RSS and remote control
points.text: A search engine queries many torrent sites at once. RSS feeds can download automatically with regex filters, and a web interface lets you run it from another device.

points.title: Fine control
points.text: You can queue and prioritize torrents and files, download pieces in order, schedule bandwidth, filter IPs and create your own torrents.

points.title: Two libtorrent builds
points.text: Each release comes in two builds using different libtorrent versions, for example 5.3.0 and 5.3.0 lt12 on Windows. If one misbehaves on your connection or disk, try the other.

points.title: Mac is barely supported
points.text: The project says macOS is barely supported because it has no active macOS developers. The Mac build trails at 5.2.3, needs macOS 13, and the Homebrew cask is disabled because it fails Apple's Gatekeeper check.

points.title: Linux: verified Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is verified as the project's own. The project also ships an AppImage built on Ubuntu 22.04.

points.title: Versions here
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 or later, x64 only, installed for the whole machine. The Windows listing keeps 48 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
